summary.title: Maximal abelian extension of a modular curve unramified outside cusps
summary.field_subfield: Number theory / arithmetic geometry (modular curves, abelian extensions)
summary.type_of_paper: Short research note / proof of a theorem
summary.executive_summary: This note addresses a question about the maximal unramified abelian coverings of modular curves over the rational numbers. The background is Mazur's theorem that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) is the geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of X0(p) itself. However, the authors observe that if one allows ramification at the cusps, a strictly larger covering becomes possible. The central result is Theorem 1.2.2, which constructs a cyclic covering X'2(p) → X0(p) of degree 2Np (twice the degree Np of the Shimura covering) whose restriction to the cuspidal locus Y0(p) is geometrically maximal unramified over Q. The construction proceeds by realizing Q(X'2(p)) as a quadratic extension of Q(X2(p)) generated by a square root of an explicitly built rational function F^2_h, where F_h is a product of generalized Dedekind eta functions. The transformation behavior of these functions under Γ0(p) is controlled via a character ψ, and the ramification at cusps is analyzed through Fourier expansions. The note also treats the special cases p = 2, 3 and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12, which requires a different construction using triplets of eta functions. The theoretical implication is that allowing cusp ramification doubles the maximal unramified abelian degree, and the method illustrates how generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) can be used to build explicit modular functions with prescribed ramification. The paper is purely theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code, and no bibliography is provided, so top_influential_citations is empty.

Executive Summary
This note addresses a question about the maximal unramified abelian coverings of modular curves over the rational numbers. The background is Mazur's theorem that the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p) is the geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of X0(p) itself. However, the authors observe that if one allows ramification at the cusps, a strictly larger covering becomes possible. The central result is Theorem 1.2.2, which constructs a cyclic covering X'2(p) → X0(p) of degree 2Np (twice the degree Np of the Shimura covering) whose restriction to the cuspidal locus Y0(p) is geometrically maximal unramified over Q. The construction proceeds by realizing Q(X'2(p)) as a quadratic extension of Q(X2(p)) generated by a square root of an explicitly built rational function F^2_h, where F_h is a product of generalized Dedekind eta functions. The transformation behavior of these functions under Γ0(p) is controlled via a character ψ, and the ramification at cusps is analyzed through Fourier expansions. The note also treats the special cases p = 2, 3 and the case p ≡ 11 mod 12, which requires a different construction using triplets of eta functions. The theoretical implication is that allowing cusp ramification doubles the maximal unramified abelian degree, and the method illustrates how generalized Dedekind eta functions (Siegel functions) can be used to build explicit modular functions with prescribed ramification. The paper is purely theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code, and no bibliography is provided, so top_influential_citations is empty.

Research Context
The setting is the theory of maximal unramified abelian coverings of curves over number fields. For a smooth geometrically integral curve Y admitting a degree one divisor, the maximal unramified abelian extension k(Y)ur,ab of its function field is well defined. The geometric part π1(Y )ab,geo of the abelian fundamental group is finite, a key structural fact. Mazur's theorem establishes the Shimura covering as the maximal unramified abelian covering of X0(p). The gap is that allowing ramification at cusps may permit a strictly larger covering than the Shimura one.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether a geometrically maximal unramified abelian covering of the cuspidal locus Y0(p) can exceed the Shimura covering X2(p) → X0(p). The hypothesis is that such a covering exists and is cyclic of degree 2Np, factoring through the Shimura covering by a degree-two cover. The predicted outcome is that this covering is geometrically maximal over Y0(p) and ramified only at cusps. The degree doubling is predicted to arise from a Z/2Z extension of the Shimura covering. The construction is predicted to rely on generalized Dedekind eta functions generating a quadratic extension.

Methodological Details
The objects of study are the modular curves X0(p) and X1(p) as smooth proper geometrically integral curves over Q. The base curve Y0(p) is the open subscheme of X0(p) obtained by removing the two cusps 0 and ∞. The Shimura covering f_p : X2(p) → X0(p) has degree Np := (p−1)/gcd(p−1,12). The target covering f'p : X'2(p) → X0(p) has degree 2Np, twice the Shimura degree. The construction assumes p is an odd prime with p ≥ 5, with p = 2, 3 handled separately. The generalized Jacobian eJ := Jac(X, D) with modulus D is a semi-abelian variety fitting in an exact sequence. The torsion module MTor := Hom(TeJ, Q/Z(1)) is a divisible torsion Gk-module. The character group LD := Hom(GD, Gm,k) is free abelian of rank rD := Σ(x∈D)[k(x):k] − 1. The abelian fundamental group satisfies π1(Y )ab,geo ≅ Hom(MµTor(−1), Q/Z). The key group Σ(f) := ker(f*: J(k) → J'(k)) controls the maximal unramified abelian subcovering. The maximal unramified abelian covering has Galois group Hom(Σ(f), Q/Z(1)). The generalized Dedekind eta function Eg is defined via an infinite product with the second Bernoulli polynomial.

Procedures And Architectures
The proof of Theorem 1.2.2 is organized into a first reduction, eta-function preparation, and the modular curve X'2(p). The first reduction shows that a degree-2Np cyclic cover satisfying condition (2) automatically satisfies condition (1). The generalized Dedekind eta function Eg satisfies Eg+N = E−g = −Eg. The eta functions transform under Γ0(N) with a root-of-unity factor ε(a,bN,c,d) and an exponential term. Products of eta functions with Σg eg ≡ 0 mod 12, Σg geg ≡ 0 mod 2, Σg g²eg ≡ 0 mod 2N are modular functions on Γ1(N). The function F_h(τ) is defined as a product of 6/ℓ powers of ℓ eta functions E_{g^j k h}. The functions F_h satisfy F_h = F_{−h} = F_{p+h}. Key Results
The main theorem constructs a cyclic covering of degree 2Np that is geometrically maximal over Y0(p). The covering f'p factors as f'p = f_p ∘ π_p with π_p a degree-two cover unramified outside cusps. The order of MµTor(−1) is either Np or 2Np, establishing the doubling possibility. The covering X'2(p) → X2(p) ramifies precisely at each cusp. The function field Q(X'2(p)) is a quadratic extension of Q(X2(p)) generated by a square root of F^2_h. The order of F^2_h at a non-cusp point is zero, so F^2_h is unramified away from cusps. The order of F^2_h at a cusp of width p is 1, contributing to odd ramification. The order of F^2_h at a cusp of width 1 is congruent to p ≡ 1 mod 2, confirming odd order. The group Γ'2(p) gives Γ0(p)/Γ'2(p) cyclic of order 2k, matching the degree 2Np. For p ≡ 11 mod 12, the triplet construction yields G^2_h a modular function on X1(p) with odd cusp order. Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The result shows that allowing cusp ramification doubles the maximal unramified abelian degree from Np to 2Np. The doubling arises because (LD ⊗ Q/Z)µ(−1) ≅ Z/2Z contributes an extra Z/2Z factor. The geometric maximality over Y0(p) follows from the isomorphism π1(Y )ab,geo ≅ Hom(MµTor(−1), Q/Z). The construction demonstrates that generalized Dedekind eta functions can build explicit modular functions with prescribed cusp ramification. The factorization through the Shimura covering shows the new covering extends Mazur's maximal unramified cover. The degree-two extension π_p is unramified outside cusps, isolating the cusp contribution to the doubling.

Contradictions And Limitations
The construction is restricted to odd primes p ≥ 5, with p = 2, 3 handled by a separate elementary argument. The case p ≡ 11 mod 12 requires a different construction, indicating methodological sensitivity to p mod 12. The exact value of the extra Z/2Z factor is not fully pinned down, leaving Np vs 2Np as a dichotomy.
